chunks: Ahmad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, a man from the Ansar married while he was in Ihram, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) invalidated his marriage.

key_terms.أنصار: Ansar, the helpers of the Prophet from Medina
key_terms.إحرام: Ihram, the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a person who is currently in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the invalidity (batl) of the marital contract for a man who marries while in the state of Ihram, a ruling derived directly from the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) annulment of the union with an Ansari man. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence for the principle that the sanctity of the pilgrimage state restricts specific worldly transactions, including marriage, rendering them void rather than merely suspended. The narration highlights the immediate legal consequence of violating the prohibitions of Ihram, emphasizing the Prophet's authoritative role in clarifying these ritual-legal intersections.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Hareyz, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A man from the Ansaars married and he was in Ihraam. So Rasool-Allahsaww invalidated his marriage’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad has narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hariz from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A man from Ansar got married in the state of Ihram, and the Messenger of Allah, considered his marriage invalid.’”
